verdict.rationale: Custom agents are documented review rules that enforce an organization's own best practices and coding standards. They can be defined in a repo-level or org-level cubic.yaml or adopted from a community library. Reviews also pick up team context files (AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, .ai/) and Confluence/Notion docs, and an HN commenter confirms the plain-English, in-repo rules approach (criticizing it, not disproving it). Missing for 10: any evidence of AST/structural pattern rules, documentation of how linked external style guides are enforced rather than used as context, and independent hands-on corroboration that custom rules are reliably enforced.
